title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Micronesia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Micronesia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Micronesia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: When a death occurs in the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), administrative duties split between national federal frameworks and the four constituent states of Chuuk, Kosrae, Pohnpei, and Yap [1][7][8]. National health and social security rules operate alongside state-level hospital reporting, State Supreme Court vital registries, and state probate courts [1][4][8][9].

steps.title: Medical certification, hospital coordination, and remains handling
steps.html:
• Obtain medical certification of cause of death from the attending physician at the relevant public hospital or health facility listed by the FSM Department of Health and Social Affairs (hsa.gov.fm): Chuuk State Hospital (+691 330-2217), Kosrae State Hospital (+691 370-3012), Pohnpei State Hospital (+691 320-2213 / 3805), or Yap State Hospital (+691 350-2110 / 3446) [1][9][12].
  • Under Title 41, Chapter 1, Section 102 of the FSM Code, public health administration regulates interments, handling of human remains, and disinterments, while Section 105 mandates collection of birth and death records [1].
  • If remains will be transported internationally into or out of the FSM, verify strict documentation and sealing protocols outlined in the FSM Embassy shipping guide (which covers certified death certificates, embalming or cremation documentation, contagious-disease clearance, and consular or transit permits) before booking air freight [10].

steps.title: State Supreme Court death registration and certified certificates
steps.html:
• File the hospital medical notification and death particulars with the Office of the Court Clerk at the relevant State Supreme Court (FSM State Supreme Court Clerks), because civil vital records in the FSM are maintained at state level rather than by a single national registry [8].
  • Use the published State Supreme Court Clerk contacts to verify filing windows, identification rules, and certified-copy fees (generally US$ 2 to US$ 3 per copy depending on the state): Chuuk Court Clerk (691) 330-2228 / 2717, Kosrae Court Clerk (691) 370-3033, Pohnpei Court Clerk (691) 320-2355 / 5667, and Yap Court Clerk (691) 350-2161 / 2162 [8].
  • Order several original certified Death Certificates immediately, as both FSM Social Security claims and financial institutions require original official copies [5][6][8].

steps.title: FSM Social Security Administration (FSMSSA) survivor and lump-sum benefits
steps.html:
• Contact FSM Social Security Administration (FSMSSA) promptly at its Kolonia headquarters (+691 320-2706 / 2708 / 4407) or through the state branch offices in Chuuk (+691 330-2200), Kosrae (+691 370-3048), Pohnpei (+691 320-2709 / 2181), or Yap (+691 350-2309 / 8489) [6][7].
  • Check eligibility for ongoing monthly benefits for a surviving spouse or unmarried dependent children (and surviving parents where applicable) if the deceased worker achieved insured status [5]. Submit the official Death Certificate, marriage certificate, children's birth certificates, and required FSMSSA claim forms [5][8].
  • Where a deceased worker was not insured for monthly survivor pensions (or no monthly survivor qualifies), check eligibility for the statutory Lump Sum Benefit equal to 4% of cumulative covered earnings (including Trust Territory and FSM Social Security earnings), minus prior benefits paid to the worker or dependants [6]. Under FSMSSA rules, any lump-sum payment follows statutory priority: surviving spouse first, then children equally (or legal guardian for minors), then parents equally, and otherwise the court-appointed legal representative [6].

steps.title: State probate, estate administration, and Title 54 tax position
steps.html:
• Probate, Will validation, and intestate estate letters are governed at the state level rather than by a uniform national probate statute (for example, Title 49 of the Pohnpei State Code governs Wills and Decedents' Estates in Pohnpei) [4]. Confirm filing requirements with the local State Supreme Court Clerk or seek intake guidance from Micronesian Legal Services Corporation (MLSC) if qualifying legal-aid representation is needed [4][8][11].
  • Check whether an employer owes accrued wages or accrued leave balances, noting that national civil servants fall under Title 52 / FSM Public Service System Regulations while private-sector employees depend on written contracts and state labor rules [3].
  • Review personal wage, gross revenue, or corporate filings governed by Title 54 of the FSM Code [2]. The national FSM tax framework under Title 54 imposes wage/salary and gross revenue taxes rather than a federal estate or inheritance tax [2].

steps.title: Consular legalisation and notifying banks and institutions
steps.html:
• Because the Federated States of Micronesia is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, certified State Supreme Court Death Certificates and court orders sent overseas require consular or diplomatic authentication rather than a Hague Apostille [13]. Confirm authentication requirements with the foreign embassy or receiving institution before dispatching originals abroad [10][13].
  • Notify domestic banks, employers, insurers, utilities, and custom/land registries in writing with certified Death Certificates and court appointment letters [4][8].
  • Retain certified copies of every FSMSSA filing, hospital record, and court receipt for multi-state or international family settlement [5][8][10].

contacts.name: FSM State Supreme Court Clerks
contacts.note: Issues certified vital records across the four states: Pohnpei (691) 320-2355/5667, Chuuk (691) 330-2228/2717, Kosrae (691) 370-3033, Yap (691) 350-2161/2162.

contacts.name: FSM Social Security Administration (FSMSSA)
contacts.note: Headquarters in Kolonia, Pohnpei (+691 320-2706/2708/4407) with state offices in Chuuk, Kosrae, Pohnpei, and Yap for survivor pensions and 4% lump-sum claims.

contacts.name: FSM Department of Health and Social Affairs
contacts.note: National health department coordinating with state hospitals in Chuuk (+691 330-2217), Kosrae (+691 370-3012), Pohnpei (+691 320-2213), and Yap (+691 350-2110).

contacts.name: Micronesian Legal Services Corporation (MLSC)
contacts.note: Provides legal-aid support for low-income residents in estate, probate, power of attorney, and guardianship matters across FSM states.
